messages.subject: Errors using "spatialDetectionHistory" function
messages.body_plain:
Hello there,

I am facing some issues with the function "spatialDetectionHistory", which I am not finding a solution, and I would appreciate very much any help.

The first issue I have faced and solved in the past, when camtrapR was still in one of the first versions. I am usnig the latest version (2.2.0) now, and managed to solve this issue in similar way. However, when I used the old version, after this fix I ran "spatialDetectionHistory" and it all worked fine. Using both versions, the error read the following:

"Error: there is a mismatch between station IDs in CTtable and rownames in camOp (length differs)"

Looking at the vignette of the latest camtrapR version, I understand that the function "cameraOperation" now attaches a suffix in the Station name (CAM), if I use two camer-traps per station, as in my case. So I created a new column in both the recordTableIndividual and the CTtable, to match the rownames of the camOp table. I attached prints of the original tables and the fixes.

head(amos2019) # CTtable before fixing the first error
head(amos2019) # CTtable after fixing the first error and adding new column "Station_Cam"

The first error above is solved, but now, I run into the following error without being able to go around:

"Error in make.capthist(captures = sdh2, traps = secr.traps, fmt = "trapID", :
failed to match some capture locations to detector sites

1. spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recTabInd, species = "Jaguatirica",
camOp = amos2019_Prob, CTtable = amos2019, output = "count",
stationCol = "Station_Cam", speciesCol = "Species", Xcol = "Utm_X",
Ycol = "Utm_Y", individualCol = "Individual", individualCovariateCols = "Sex",

2. make.capthist(captures = sdh2, traps = secr.traps, fmt = "trapID",
noccasions = noccasions, bysession = TRUE)

3. stop("failed to match some capture locations ", "to detector sites") "

My codes are:

amos2019_Prob <- cameraOperation(CTtable = amos2019,
stationCol = "Station",
cameraCol = "Camera",
setupCol = "data_inicial",
retrievalCol = "data_final",
writecsv = T,
hasProblems = TRUE,
byCamera = TRUE,
#allCamsOn = FALSE,
outDir = "C:/CameraTrapPicSF/2019_Amostragem",
dateFormat = "%d/%m/%Y"
)

amos2019_Prob[1:6,1:6]

recTabInd <- recordTableIndividual(inDir = "C:/Jaguatirica",
hasStationFolders = FALSE,
IDfrom = "directory",
cameraID = "filename",
camerasIndependent = FALSE,
minDeltaTime = 60,
deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",
timeZone = "America/Campo_Grande",
stationCol = "Station",
writecsv = TRUE,
outDir = "C:/CameraTrapPicSF/stragemFinal_2019",
removeDuplicateRecords = TRUE,
returnFileNamesMissingTags = TRUE
)

head(recTabInd ) # before fixing the first error

head(recTabInd ) # after fixing the first error and adding new column "Station_Cam"

JaguaSDH <- spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recTabInd,
species = "Jaguatirica",
camOp = amos2019_Prob,
CTtable = amos2019,
output = "count",
stationCol = "Station_Cam",
speciesCol = "Species",
Xcol = "Utm_X",
Ycol = "Utm_Y",
individualCol = "Individual",
individualCovariateCols = "Sex",
recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal",
recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
occasionLength = 1,
day1 = "station",
includeEffort = TRUE,
scaleEffort = FALSE,
binaryEffort = FALSE,
timeZone = "America/Campo_Grande",
makeRMarkInput = FALSE
)

I appreciate any help!
Cheers,
Henrique

messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Using agouti output files in camtrapR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jim,
thank you for informing, that sounds good. I haven't tried your package yet, but appreciate the effort and will give it a try.
A possibly unrelated question to you, the original poster privately shared the output of Agouti (observation and deployment csv files) and I found several issues with these. While I don't know if these may be artefacts from manual data processing after export from Agouti, I'd like to bring them to your attention. We can discuss this separately if more appropriate.

observations:
timestamp format is not consistent (some are with time zone, others without)
deployments:
some rows have identical setup and retrieval date and time (thus a deployment length of 0)
there are multiple deployments at the same location & same camera. I suppose that is intended and means the camera malfunctioned or or sampling was interrupted. Does your package convert these to the ProblemX_from/to columns as used by camtrapR? (I am aware the ProblemX columns are not ideal from a data management point of view, but still)
timestamp is not consistent (some are with time zone, others without; some of the entries with time zone are -06:00, others -07:00)

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Problem Renaming and exporting Images
messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio,
and apologies for the extremely late reply.
The files beginning with "._" are specific to iOS and are listed by list.files() in R, which causes problems. See
https://www.cnet.com/tech/computing/invisible-files-with-prefix-are-created-on-some-shared-volumes-and-external-disks/

I am not familiar with iOS, so I can't say why it only happens in one station.

The other message about "no new images to be copied" means that the 138 images you wish to copy already exist in the new location " wd_images_raw_renamed " and are therefore not copied.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Occumulti error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sofia,
sorry for the late reply. I'd need to see the actual data, but the error in node z[1,17] suggests a problem with calculating occupancy probability for species 1 at station 17. Missing covariate value maybe?

z[species, station] is the binary occupancy status, which is created from the occupancy probability psi [species, station], which in turn comes from the occupancy formula (where only the covariate values are station-specific).

In any case, it doesn't make sense that only the model for one covariate fails and the others run ok. So this suggests some problem with the input data rather than the model structure.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to set occasion length to minutes?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a way to set occasion length to minutes?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
sorry, occasions shorter than one day are currently not supported. It would require some larger changes in the code of both detectionHistory and cameraOperation which I currently don't have the time for.
One can potentially do it manually in R, e.g. the following is a very rough sketch for hourly occasions. But it only uses the first and last record as start/end occasion (not the camera operation times), hence the detection history dimensions would differ between species, and it does not account for trapping effort (no NAs).
I added a proper implementation to the to-do list, but don't know when I'll get to it.
Best,
Jürgen

data(recordTableSample)

recordTableSample$hour <- lubridate::hour(recordTableSample$DateTimeOriginal)
recordTableSample$date_hour <- paste(as.numeric(as.Date(recordTableSample$Date)), recordTableSample$hour)

tmp <- expand.grid(seq(as.numeric(min(as.Date(recordTableSample$Date))),
    as.numeric(max(as.Date(recordTableSample$Date)))),
    0:23)

recordTableSample$date_hour <- factor(recordTableSample$date_hour, levels = sort(paste(tmp$Var1, tmp$Var2)))

dethist <- reshape2::dcast(recordTableSample, Station ~ date_hour,drop = F)
rownames(dethist) <- dethist$Station
dethist$Station <- NULL

dethist2 <- (dethist >= 1) * 1
dethist2

Hi,
normally such workarounds should not be necessary. For spatialDetectionHistory(), I think one needs to set byCamera= FALSE in cameraOperation. Then there will be no "CAM" prefix in the station names, no need for manual edits and no mismatch in station IDs

If that is not the case, would you be able to share a short reproducible example please?
Thank you,
Jürgen
